en: The Sūtra on the Vajra Dhāraṇī of the Destruction of Phenomenal Characteristics, spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Imperial Edict by the Tripitaka Master Śaraba, Grand Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Minister of Education.
Thus have I heard.
At one time, the Bhagavān was at Vajrapada.
At that time, the Tathāgata sustained himself through his supernormal power.
Once Vajrapāṇi’s body had become vajra,
he entered the Vajra-samādhi on that very day.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi...
Relying upon the spiritual power of the Buddha and the sustaining power of all Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas,
Vajrakrodha proclaimed this most sublime Vajra-hṛdaya-dhāraṇī.
It is unceasing, indestructible, and firm in its ultimate reality;
it is incapable of being obstructed and free from any fear or retreat.
It strikes terror into all sentient beings.
It is able to subdue the afflictions of sentient beings;
it cuts off all vidyā-mantras and suppresses all vidyā-mantras;
furthermore, it crushes all conditioned formations and can destroy the practices of others.
It crushes all māras and liberates them from the grasp of māras;
it encompasses all classes of bhūtas and further causes all those who practice vidyā-mantras [to succeed].
May those who have not yet attained accomplishment attain it;
may those who have already attained it not let their efforts go to waste;
and may all their aspirations be fulfilled according to their wishes.
It can also protect all sentient beings, pacifying calamities and increasing prosperity;
furthermore, it can restrain all malevolent sentient beings who are deluded and distressed—
all of this is through the power of the *dhāraṇī* divine mantra.
Vajrapāṇi, empowered by the Buddha’s spiritual authority, then spoke this mantra:
“May all sinful karma be completely purified; May all suffering be utterly eliminated.
This is the root of all sūtras, Adorned with the marks of wondrous virtue.”
Sentient beings suffer the impairment of their faculties, the exhaustion of life, untimely death,
and the lack of abundance; they are abandoned by the gods,
reviled by their kin and friends, and provoke the anger of brahmins.
Afflicted by harm and discord, lacking wealth and beset by turmoil, anxiety, grief, and the oppression of suffering;
encountering calamities, poverty, hardship, malevolent stars, and curses; they are harmed by various demons.
Those who are pregnant and burdened by grief, those who have seen inauspicious dreams,
and those who have bathed until they are completely pure— should listen to this most excellent sutra.
Those with pure and virtuous minds should likewise don clean and fresh garments.
By relying on the Buddha’s profound conduct, those who receive and uphold this sutra—
through its majestic spiritual power— shall cause all the sufferings of illness and other afflictions of those sentient beings to be completely extinguished.
May merit and longevity both increase; may one remain far removed from all defilements of sin.
Like pearls, mustard seeds, fragrant vines, and grasses; like flawless jewels, sandalwood, jade, and the vajra;
like flowers, the pure water of Yama, and the golden vase.
Alternatively, one may use a silver flask, tied with pure colored silk;
recite the mantra of the Diamond of Destroying Appearances (*Vajra-bheda*) twenty-one times—
or even up to one hundred and eight times— and the king shall always bathe.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Vajra Dhāraṇī of the Destruction of Characteristics.
